title: fix(messaging): read every preference row of a topic in pages, not an unordered first 10,000
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-support-ai"} -->
_Requested by **Yibo Wang** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01BVUyyPie8gHwoPM18iABwB?thread=cmsg_01BVUyyPie8gHwoPM18iABwBH348tBEd1BK8EHjKGRA6r7)_

Fixes #35136

repo:objectstack#3 · os-support-ai · session_01WGufzhJib2jSynT4AV2A54

## 维护者速读

- 发通知时，系统现在会把一个组织在该主题下的全部偏好设置读完再决定是否送达；以前超过一万条时会随机漏读一部分。普通组织用户无感。
- 属于「通知渠道」专题：大组织里成员自己设的退订、汇总、免打扰可能被漏读，通知照发。
- 若出错，读偏好失败时仍按原规则全部送达并记一条警告，不会吞掉通知；改动只在服务端读取逻辑，可直接回滚。
- 无。

## What changes

`PreferenceResolver.loadRows` (the preference filter `emit` runs before writing deliveries) read an organization's `sys_notification_preference` rows for the event's topic and for `*` with one `find` each, `limit: 10000`, no order, then filtered by recipient in memory. Past 10,000 rows for one topic an undefined subset was dropped, so a recipient's own opt-out, digest or quiet hours could be missed and the event delivered as if the row did not exist.

**Route chosen: bounded pages, read to the end.** Each topic is now walked with the shared `keysetWalk` (`@objectstack/types`): pages of `PREFERENCE_PAGE_SIZE` (1,000) rows ordered by `id`, each page seeking past the last `id` (`$and` of the caller's equality `where` and `id $gt cursor`). Every page is read; only the recipients' rows and the admin-global default (empty `user_id`) are kept, so memory is bounded by the recipients, not by the organization. Still equality on `topic` plus a seek on `id`: no IN, as the old comment required.

Why not the other two routes the card allows:
- **Per-recipient equality** (the `effectiveFor` shape) costs 2 reads per recipient. An `org:members` broadcast to 5,000 people would make about 10,000 reads per emit, where today it makes 2. Paging keeps 2 reads for any organization under 1,000 rows per topic, and adds reads only where the old code was wrong.
- **A refusal on its own** (read cap+1, throw) lands in `filter`'s fail-open path. Every emit in a large organization would then ignore everyone's preferences, for good. That is worse than the bug.

**Interaction with fail-open.** `loadRows` throws in one new case only: the walk cannot move past a FULL page (a reader that ignores the seek returns the same page again, or a row has no `id`). It refuses that partial set instead of filtering on it. `filter` catches the throw like any failed read: every channel is kept and `[preferences] lookup for topic 'T' failed (...); delivering all (fail-open)` is logged at `warn`. That is the resolver's existing rule ("a preference outage must never silently swallow notifications"), unchanged. A short last page with no `id` is complete (the source answered everything left), so it is not refused. Production drivers apply the seek (the SqlDriver pin below runs it), so this branch is a guard against a reader that does not, not a path a real database takes.

No exported type, option or signature changes (L1 M1). The tests shrink the page through `setPreferencePageSizeForTests`, a module-level seam the package entry does not re-export, so the built `dist/index.d.ts` has no page-size option: `PreferenceResolverOptions` and the class declaration have the same shape as on `main`. `preference-user-conversion.ts`: only its `PASS_LIMIT` doc comment changes. It said "the same ceiling `PreferenceResolver.loadRows` reads with", which this PR makes false. The conversion's logic is not touched (see Acceptance notes).

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## Tests

New file `preference-rows-paged-read-35136.integration.test.ts`, named for this card as the seat's order asked, so the shared `preference-resolver.test.ts` is left alone while #36369 runs in this package. Its fake engine ignores `orderBy`, `limit` and the seek, so it cannot show paging:
- a double that applies equality, `$and`, `$gt`, `orderBy` and `limit` like a driver: the recipient's own email mute sits on page 3 of pages of 2 and is found. The test checks its own premise (page 1 does not hold the row) and pins the page sequence and the seek `where`;
- default page size: the reads ask for `PREFERENCE_PAGE_SIZE`, never 10,000;
- a reader that ignores the seek: the walk stops on the repeated page, and `filter` fails open with one `warn` rather than filtering on page 1;
- a real `ObjectQL` / `SqlDriver` (better-sqlite3) file database with pages of 2: the recipient's mute (page 3) and the organization's `*` default both apply, and the same user's opposite row in another organization is not read.

**Ablation** (the test imports `src`, so no build is in the path). Made with `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` on the committed fix. It replaced `lastPage = page.length;` with `if (lastPage > 0) break; lastPage = (page.length);`, so only the first page is read: anchor 1→0, blob `83c62c4ffecb`→`08e7d52cf174`. Result: **3 of 4 red**: page-3 row, refusal and real driver. The default-page-size pin stays green, as expected. Restore: blob == HEAD and `git diff HEAD` empty.

## Acceptance notes

- `preference-user-conversion.ts`'s pass loop still reads 10,000 rows per pass, unordered. It ends when a pass returns no row it has not seen. With more than 10,000 `'*'` rows LEFT AS STORED (failed conversions), a pass could return only seen rows and stop before rows it never read. That needs over 10,000 failed admin-default conversions. Noted, not changed. carrier: none.
- `preference-digest-conversion.ts:62` has the same `PASS_LIMIT = 10000`. It is the file #36369 owns, so it is left alone.
- `slack-links.ts:265` reads `sys_channel_user_link` for one account with `limit: 10000` and no order: the same shape on a different object. Not measured, not changed. carrier: none.
- With no organization (neither the producer nor the event row names one), the read stays unscoped, as before and as `emit`'s step-3b comment states.
